title: Introduce smart presubmit prober and lean release adapter to speed CI feedback
author: Ria Patel
description:
Context: CI feedback latency and noisy presubmit runs have been a recurring developer friction point. This PR introduces a lightweight presubmit prober that detects change scope and schedules a minimal set of lint/test shards in a stage-aware fashion, plus a small 'release adapter' shim to decouple release hooks from strong CI invariants. The goal is to reduce developer iteration time without sacrificing coverage.

What this PR does (high level): 
- Adds a presubmit prober service that inspects changed paths, runs a fast heuristic to pick required lint/test profiles, and emits a scoped job matrix.
- Splits lint into stage-aware profiles (quickstyle, type-only, full-lint) to enable fast fastpath feedback.
- Introduces a release adapter that runs final release-orchestration steps asynchronously and provides a stable API for release tooling so main CI is not blocked by transient release hooks.
- Provides docs, devcontainer scripts, and a small golang-based prober binary for hermetic local runs.

Checklist: 
- [x] Add presubmit prober service and CLI (ci/prober). 
- [x] Update .github workflows to use the prober output for presubmit matrices. 
- [x] Split lint profiles and add quickstyle runner. 
- [x] Add release adapter shim and backward-compatible env flags. 
- [x] Add observability: presubmit probe metrics and quickpath hit rate. 
- [x] Run dogfood on redwood/* and redwood-sdk-* repos for 48h.

Testing notes: 
- Dogfooded across core monorepo for two working days; observed median presubmit latency drop from 12m -> 5m for small changes. Quickpath (quickstyle only) hit rate ~42% on typical PRs. 
- CI runs: full integration and nightly smoke passed. A lint runner flake in early iterations was fixed by tightening the module cache initialization. 

Rollout plan: 
1. Merge to main behind feature flag PROBER_ENABLED=false. 
2. Enable for SDK repos (redwood-sdk-python/ts/go) for 72h and monitor quickpath metrics. 
3. Gradual opt-in across monorepo by team using per-repo config. 
4. Remove flag after 4 weeks of stable metrics.

Backward compatibility: release adapter uses environment opt-ins and keeps existing release hooks unmodified unless RELEASE_ADAPTER=enabled is set.

Motivation and tradeoffs: This PR trades a small amount of additional infra (prober binary + metrics) for large developer productivity gains. We preserve safety by keeping slow full runs as fallback and by retaining the previous full-matrix behavior behind a flag.

Related: ENG-1729 (presubmit speed initiative), ENG-2104 (release automation hygiene), SUP-981 (customer incident prompting quicker release decoupling).

chore(ci): split lint into quickstyle/type/full profiles and wire prober output to workflow matrix
feat(release): add lightweight release adapter shim and retries for webhooks
docs(ci): add presubmit-prober.md and rollout guide
fix(ci): stabilize lint runner module cache initialization to avoid flake

Ria Patel: Prober includes a fallback threshold: if changed file count > 25 or touched core/ infra/ release/*, we emit full matrix. Added a test to assert that behavior.
Sofia Ramirez: LGTMed after seeing dogfood metrics and the added observability. Small nits on docs fixed.
Marcus Chen: Approved. Will squash+merge after green CI.
release_notes: Introduce a presubmit prober that reduces presubmit matrix size by running scoped lint/test profiles. Add a release adapter shim to decouple release hooks from core CI. Opt-in via PROBER_ENABLED/RELEASE_ADAPTER flags. Impact: faster feedback for small changes; no breaking behavior by default.
